name: disable-comments
notes: Adapter-authoring probe 2026-09-14: inspected the official WordPress.org Disable Comments 2.9.0 artifact (SHA-256 17bc60cc872d77f36a88fa27638bb2e15774bdd15418d966559c32cbbfe3e2c5). The range is intentionally limited to the observed release; widening it requires another artifact probe.

disable-comments.php loads the site option disable_comments_options and its settings writer persists one shared array. This capsule narrows that blob to five reviewed toggles: remove_everywhere, remove_xmlrpc_comments, remove_rest_API_comments, show_existing_comments, and enable_exclude_by_role.

The five selected values are consumed as boolean or integer toggles by Disable_Comments filters. They are authored site policy, not entity references, credentials, counters, version markers, or cache state; lint_ok records that these numeric toggle values must not be mistaken for local IDs.

disabled_post_types, extra_post_types, conditional_rules, allowed_comment_types, and blocked_comment_types remain unclaimed because they carry post-type, taxonomy-term, template, or comment-type semantics that need separate native and reference evidence. Network settings, counters, review state, user metadata, and uninstall behavior are also outside this experimental slice.

The plugin's network option path and sitewide settings are excluded by WPrism's single-site boundary. No interpreter, provider, regenerator, entity declaration, or engine feature is needed for this source-read slice.

enable_exclude_by_role.note: Disable_Comments::is_exclude_by_role() treats this as a boolean feature toggle.

remove_everywhere.note: Disable_Comments::is_remove_everywhere() consumes this as a site-wide boolean toggle.

show_existing_comments.note: Disable_Comments uses this boolean presentation choice when existing comments remain stored.
